cards.name: MCP — Model Context Protocol
cards.desc: Anthropic's connection standard — lets AI talk to any tool, database, or API through one unified protocol. Often called 'USB-C for AI'.
cards.detail:
Agent ↔ Tool communication · The "USB-C for AI" · Adopted by OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Cursor, Replit, Sourcegraph
MCP Apps (Jan 2026): New extension — tools return interactive UI (dashboards, forms) directly in conversation
Skills over MCP: Experimental — skill discovery & distribution via MCP primitives
whenToUse: tool integration for LLMs
connecting AI apps to external data sources
building standardized AI plugins
cross-platform tool sharing
whenNotToUse: agent-to-agent communication (use A2A)
simple REST API calls without AI context

cards.name: A2A — Agent2Agent Protocol
cards.desc: Google's protocol — lets AI agents communicate and collaborate with each other, regardless of their underlying framework.
cards.detail:
Agent ↔ Agent communication · Complements MCP (MCP = tools, A2A = agents)
Agent Cards: JSON-based capability descriptors for agent discovery
v0.3 (Jul 2025): gRPC support, security cards, expanded Python SDK
150+ organizations support · Linux Foundation hosted
cards.note: 💡 Dùng MCP cho tools, A2A cho agents — 2 protocol bổ sung nhau, không thay thế!
whenToUse: agent-to-agent communication
cross-framework agent collaboration
enterprise multi-agent workflows
multi-vendor agent interop
whenNotToUse: tool integration for LLMs (use MCP)
single-agent applications

cards.name: LangGraph
cards.desc: Low-level framework from the LangChain team for stateful, long-running agents — graphs of nodes and edges with durable execution and human-in-the-loop.
cards.detail: LangGraph is the LangChain team's low-level orchestration framework for stateful agents, for Python and JavaScript (MIT). You model an agent as a graph of state, nodes and edges, with conditional routing, cycles and multi-agent or hierarchical setups. Durable execution lets runs resume after failures; short-term and long-term memory persist across steps and sessions; human-in-the-loop lets you inspect and edit state at any point. Tracing and debugging run through LangSmith, with Studio as a visual IDE. Hosted deployment — formerly LangGraph Platform — is now called LangSmith Deployment, with cloud, hybrid and self-hosted options. Used in production by companies such as Klarna, Replit, Uber, LinkedIn and Elastic.
whenToUse: Stateful, multi-step agent workflows
Complex control flow with branching and loops
Human-in-the-loop approval steps
Long-running agents that must survive failures (durable execution)
whenNotToUse: Simple single-call LLM tasks
No need to persist state between steps
Team unfamiliar with graph-based programming

cards.name: CrewAI
cards.desc: Python framework for teams of role-based AI agents (Crews) plus event-driven Flows for production control — MCP and A2A built in.
cards.detail: CrewAI is an MIT-licensed Python framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous agents. Crews group agents with roles, goals and tasks that run in a sequential or hierarchical process (a manager agent delegates); Flows add event-driven, stateful control — conditions, loops and routing — around crews for production apps. Memory, knowledge sources and checkpointing are built in; agents can use MCP servers (stdio, SSE, Streamable HTTP), and A2A is a first-class delegation primitive, so agents can call or serve remote agents. The commercial CrewAI AMP (Agent Management Platform, formerly CrewAI Enterprise) adds managed deployment from GitHub or the CLI, the no-code Crew Studio, tracing, webhooks and a tool repository, in the cloud or on-prem.
whenToUse: Multi-agent orchestration with clear roles
Role-based AI teams collaborating on one task
Production workflows mixing deterministic Flows with autonomous Crews
Delegating work to remote agents over A2A
whenNotToUse: Simple single-agent tasks
Non-Python stack
Hard real-time, low-latency requirements

cards.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
cards.desc: Microsoft's open-source framework for production agents and multi-agent workflows in .NET and Python — the direct successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel
cards.detail:
Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) is Microsoft's open-source (MIT) framework for building, orchestrating and operating AI agents in .NET and Python, with a Go SDK in preview in a separate repository. Microsoft describes it as the direct successor to both AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, built by the same teams, and publishes migration guides from each; version 1.0 shipped in April 2026 with stable APIs and long-term support. Agents call tools and MCP servers; graph-based workflows coordinate agents and functions in sequential, concurrent, handoff and group-chat patterns, with state management for long-running and human-in-the-loop runs. It adds middleware, OpenTelemetry tracing, declarative YAML agents, a developer UI, A2A support and optional hosting of agents on Microsoft Foundry. If you run AutoGen today, this is where Microsoft points you next.

Works well with: MCP · A2A · Azure / Microsoft Foundry · OpenTelemetry
whenToUse: You are building production agents or multi-agent workflows in .NET or Python
You are migrating from AutoGen or Semantic Kernel
You need workflows with checkpointing, human-in-the-loop and OpenTelemetry tracing
whenNotToUse: Your stack is TypeScript-only — see Mastra
You want the smallest possible SDK for a single agent — see OpenAI Agents SDK
You need a full Go SDK today (Go is in preview)

cards.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
cards.desc: OpenAI's lightweight, provider-agnostic agent SDK for Python and TypeScript — handoffs, guardrails, sessions and tracing built in.
cards.detail: The OpenAI Agents SDK (MIT) is a small set of primitives for building agentic apps in Python, with a separate TypeScript/JavaScript SDK. Agents use tools and hand off to other agents or call them as tools; guardrails validate inputs and outputs in parallel; sessions keep conversation history across runs; human-in-the-loop pauses runs for approval. Built-in tracing feeds OpenAI's evaluation and fine-tuning tools. Tools include Python functions, MCP servers (local and remote) and OpenAI hosted tools; realtime voice agents and container-based sandbox agents cover longer tasks. Works with the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs and with other model providers. The SDK evolves quickly, so APIs can change between releases.
whenToUse: Lightweight multi-agent workflows with few abstractions
Handoffs between specialized agents
Built-in tracing and guardrails from day one
whenNotToUse: You need a full workflow or graph engine
You want tracing outside the OpenAI platform by default (tracing defaults to OpenAI)
You need a no-code agent builder UI

cards.name: Google ADK
cards.desc: Google's open-source, code-first Agent Development Kit for Python, TypeScript, Go, Java and Kotlin — graph workflows, A2A and MCP.
cards.detail: ADK (Apache-2.0) is Google's toolkit for building, evaluating and deploying agents, now available in five languages: Python, Go, TypeScript, Java and Kotlin. Agents use tools and sub-agents; graph-based workflows add routing, parallel steps and human-in-the-loop. Every SDK includes an MCP client, and A2A support lets agents expose or call remote agents. adk eval tests agents against golden datasets. It is optimized for Gemini but model-agnostic, with adapters for other providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI (and LiteLLM in Python). Run it anywhere, or deploy to Cloud Run, GKE or Gemini Enterprise Agent Runtime (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine). Docs live at adk.dev.

sources.title: Google Cloud — One ADK, five languages

whenToUse: Building agents in the Google Cloud / Gemini ecosystem
Teams that want one framework across Python, TypeScript, Go, Java or Kotlin
Hierarchical multi-agent systems that talk over A2A
whenNotToUse: You don't use Google Cloud or Gemini and prefer a provider-neutral community framework
You only need a very simple single-agent script
You want the widest third-party integration ecosystem

cards.name: LlamaIndex
cards.desc: Open-source Python framework for agents and RAG over your own data — connectors, indexes, query engines and agent workflows.
cards.detail: LlamaIndex (MIT) is a Python framework for building LLM apps and agents over private data. LlamaHub connectors load documents and data; indexes (vector, property graph and more) and storage back query engines, retrievers, rerankers and routers; agents, tools and multi-agent patterns run on top, with human-in-the-loop, MCP (use MCP tools or expose workflows as MCP), instrumentation and evaluation modules. Hundreds of integration packages cover LLMs, embeddings and vector stores, and it integrates with LangChain. The company's commercial focus has shifted to LlamaParse, a paid document parsing and extraction platform that plugs into the framework; the TypeScript library (LlamaIndex.TS) was archived in April 2026.
whenToUse: Connecting LLMs to your own data sources
Building RAG pipelines over documents
Structured data extraction from unstructured text
Agent workflows that need data retrieval
whenNotToUse: No custom data integration needed
Simple prompt-response without retrieval
TypeScript/JavaScript projects — LlamaIndex.TS is no longer maintained

cards.name: AgentScope
cards.desc: Open-source Python agent framework with a ready-made agent service — ReAct agents, agent teams, MCP and A2A, sandboxed tools
cards.detail:
AgentScope is an open-source (Apache 2.0) framework for building and running LLM agents. Version 2.0 (2026) rebuilt it around agentic models: a ReAct agent loop with structured output and interruption, a toolkit that manages Python tools, MCP servers and skills, context compaction, middleware hooks, fine-grained permissions with human-in-the-loop, and isolated execution in local, Docker or cloud sandboxes. Long-term memory has switchable backends (ReMe, Mem0). Beyond the SDK it ships an agent service — a FastAPI backend with a web UI — that adds multi-tenant sessions, leader–worker agent teams, a RAG service, IM channels and scheduling. It can call remote agents over A2A, supports major model providers including local models through Ollama, and has an experimental realtime voice agent. This card covers the Python framework (Python 3.11+); a Java edition is developed in a separate repository.

Works well with: MCP · A2A · Ollama · Docker
whenToUse: You want a Python framework plus a ready-made service layer (sessions, web UI, teams) for agent apps
You need agents that run tools and code in sandboxes with permission controls
You want MCP tools and A2A remote agents in one framework
whenNotToUse: You want a minimal SDK with few abstractions — see OpenAI Agents SDK or Pydantic AI
Your stack is TypeScript-only — see Mastra
You need graph-based durable workflows as the core model — see LangGraph or Microsoft Agent Framework

cards.name: Browser-Use
cards.desc: Open-source Python library that lets AI agents use a web browser with any LLM — plus Browser Use Cloud for hosted browsers and agents.
cards.detail: Browser Use (MIT) is a Python library for AI browser agents: an agent navigates pages, clicks, fills forms and completes multi-step web tasks, using models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local models via Ollama, or Browser Use's own model. You can add custom tools and system prompts, and reuse logins through Chrome or cloud profiles. A local MCP server exposes it to tools such as Claude Code and Cursor. Browser Use Cloud adds a hosted agent API with Python and TypeScript SDKs and cloud browser infrastructure (stealth browsers, live view, recordings) usable from Playwright, Puppeteer or CDP, billed by usage. Best for: web automation and data extraction where no API exists.
whenToUse: AI agents that need to interact with websites
Extracting data from complex, dynamic pages
End-to-end web workflow automation
whenNotToUse: Tasks that don't involve a browser
A clean API integration is available
You can't run Chromium locally and don't want paid cloud browsers

cards.name: Pydantic AI
cards.desc: Type-safe Python agent framework from the Pydantic team — validated structured output, many model providers, evals, durable execution and MCP.
cards.detail: Pydantic AI (MIT) brings a FastAPI-like, type-safe developer experience to agents: typed dependency injection, validated structured outputs and model-agnostic agents across many providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, OpenRouter and more). It includes Pydantic Evals and Pydantic Graph, a capabilities/harness layer for planning, subagents and cross-session memory, durable execution via Temporal, DBOS, Prefect and others, human-in-the-loop tool approval, an MCP client and server, and A2A through the fasta2a package. Observability uses OpenTelemetry, with Pydantic Logfire (a separate paid product) as the closest integration. Docs moved to pydantic.dev/docs/ai.
whenToUse: Type-safe, structured agent outputs
Projects already using the Pydantic ecosystem
Model-agnostic agent development
Agents that need strict input/output validation
whenNotToUse: Non-Python projects
Visual or low-code agent building

cards.name: Mastra
cards.desc: TypeScript framework for AI agents and apps from the team behind Gatsby — agents, graph workflows, memory, RAG, evals, MCP and A2A.
cards.detail: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for AI-powered applications and agents, built by the founders of Gatsby (YC-backed). Agents use tools and memory; a graph workflow engine (.then(), .branch(), .parallel()) supports suspend and resume for human-in-the-loop; model routing reaches dozens of providers. RAG, evals/scorers and observability are built in, along with MCP servers and client, and A2A in both directions. Embed it in React, Next.js or Node apps or run it as a standalone server; Studio helps develop and debug locally. Licensing is open-core: the framework is Apache-2.0, while ee/ features fall under the Mastra Enterprise License (free for development, paid in production). The managed Mastra Platform offers hosting with a free Starter tier.
whenToUse: TypeScript AI applications and agents
Agent workflows that need evals and observability built in
Embedding agents in React, Next.js or Node apps
Rapid prototyping in a TypeScript stack
whenNotToUse: Python-only teams
Plain JavaScript projects that won't adopt TypeScript
You want every feature under an open-source license (ee/ features are commercial)

cards.name: Claude.ai (Web)
cards.desc: Anthropic's chat workspace — with memory, web search, Claude Cowork, and team plugins/connectors for enterprise workflows.
cards.detail: Anthropic's primary chat workspace. Features Projects for organizing conversations, built-in web search, cross-session memory, and Artifacts (create code, documents, charts directly in chat). Supports Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, and Haiku 4.5. Extended ecosystem: Claude Cowork is a research-preview desktop agent for knowledge work that brings Claude Code's agentic capabilities beyond coding. Teams can customize Claude with plugins and connectors for specialized workflows, distribute them through private plugin marketplaces, and orchestrate work across Excel and PowerPoint.

cards.detail: The world's most popular AI chat by OpenAI with hundreds of millions of weekly users. Features GPTs (custom chatbots), Custom Instructions (personalization), web browsing, DALL-E (image generation), Code Interpreter, and plugin ecosystem. Supports GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o1, o3. cards.name: Claude-Mem
cards.desc: Plugin that gives Claude Code persistent long-term memory — automatically records experience, compresses intelligently, and remembers across sessions.
cards.detail:
Architecture: 5 lifecycle hooks (SessionStart → UserPromptSubmit → PostToolUse → Summary → SessionEnd)
RAD (Retrieval Augmented Decisions): a new open standard — RAG captures knowledge, RAD captures intelligence
Endless Mode: ~1000 tool uses (vs 50 default), O(N) scaling
whenToUse: Cần giữ context giữa các phiên Claude Code
Dự án lớn cần session continuity và compound learning
whenNotToUse: Chỉ dùng sessions ngắn, độc lập
Cần memory cho non-Claude agents

cards.name: Other Memory Systems

subItems.title: CLAUDE.md (native)
subItems.desc: Bộ nhớ tích hợp sẵn của Claude Code: 4 cấp hierarchy (user → project → local → managed). Import files với @path syntax.

subItems.title: OpenClaw Session Memory
subItems.desc: Per-agent session files + SOUL.md personality. Cross-session nhưng isolated per workspace.

subItems.title: ByteRover
subItems.desc: Self-improving memory layer cho AI coding agents. Unify "vibe-coding" memories across projects & teams qua MCP.

subItems.title: MemGPT / Letta
subItems.desc: Stateful agents with persistent memory — kiến trúc tiered memory (core/archival/recall).

cards.detail: Beyond Claude-Mem, several other memory systems exist: MemGPT/Letta — self-manages context windows like an OS manages RAM, with a paging mechanism. Mem0 — memory layer for LLM apps using vector search. Zep — long-term memory for chatbots with auto-summarization. ByteRover — searches memory from GitHub repositories. Each system tackles a different aspect of the 'AI that remembers' problem.
whenToUse: Agent cần nhớ user preferences qua nhiều conversations
Xây dựng AI assistant có personalization dài hạn
whenNotToUse: Chỉ cần short-term context trong 1 session
Ứng dụng stateless không cần nhớ user history

cards.name: MemOS
cards.desc: Unified memory operating system for LLMs — manages memory via MemCube with short-term and long-term support
cards.detail: MemOS provides a standardized memory layer architecture for AI agents with MemCube — the basic memory unit containing both data and metadata. Supports multiple memory types (parametric, activation, long-term) and integrates with popular frameworks. ~6.9K stars, active development (v2.0.4, Jan 2026). Unique for providing a unified memory interface that Mem0/Zep haven't fully addressed.
whenToUse: Cần persistent skill memory cho agent cross-task reuse
Xây hệ thống multi-agent cần shared memory layer
whenNotToUse: Chỉ cần simple key-value memory
Project nhỏ không cần memory OS phức tạp

cards.name: Universal Agent Skills
cards.desc: Skills are .md files with instructions for AI agents — simple yet effective, runnable on any AI coding tool.
cards.detail: The Agent Skills ecosystem is booming — Anthropic has standardized the SKILL.md format to teach AI agents specialized abilities. Antigravity Awesome Skills (631+ skills, V4.0) is the largest collection, supporting Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode. VoltAgent offers 200+ skills from official teams (Stripe, Cloudflare, Hugging Face, Sentry). Simple setup: npx antigravity-awesome-skills or clone into .agent/skills/.
whenToUse: Khi cần mở rộng khả năng của AI agents với kiến thức chuyên biệt
Khi muốn tạo reusable workflows cho team
Khi cần chuẩn hóa quy trình phát triển với coding agents
whenNotToUse: Khi cần logic phức tạp hơn instructions — dùng MCP servers
Khi cần custom runtime hoặc API integration — dùng frameworks

cards.name: Superpowers
cards.desc: Agent-style skills framework for Claude Code — automatically activates the right skills based on context.
cards.detail: Superpowers is the leading skills framework for Claude Code with 20+ built-in skills: brainstorming, TDD, debugging, code review, git worktrees... Skills auto-activate based on context — for example, the systematic-debugging skill triggers automatically when debugging. Supports subagent-driven development: splits tasks into subtasks, each handled by a subagent then reviewed. Claude can run autonomously for hours without intervention. Install via Claude Code's plugin marketplace. Also supports Codex and OpenCode.
whenToUse: Khi muốn structured software development workflow cho coding agents
Khi cần TDD enforcement và code review tự động
Khi muốn subagent-driven development với review gates
whenNotToUse: Khi chỉ cần quick code generation đơn giản
Khi dự án quá nhỏ cho full TDD workflow

cards.name: Agents (wshobson)
cards.desc: Collection of 112 agents + 146 skills + 73 specialized plugins for Claude Code — the largest to date.
cards.detail: Agents is a production-ready system combining 112 specialized AI agents, 16 workflow orchestrators, 146 skills, and 79 development tools — all organized into 73 single-purpose plugins for Claude Code. Agents are categorized by domain: architecture, languages, infrastructure, security, data/AI, documentation, business operations, SEO. Install individual plugins to optimize token usage. Supports automatic Sonnet + Haiku routing based on task complexity.
whenToUse: Khi cần multi-agent orchestration với specialized domain agents
Khi muốn plugin architecture mô-đun — chỉ load agents cần thiết
Khi cần workflow orchestrators cho full-stack, security, ML pipelines
whenNotToUse: Khi chỉ cần 1-2 skills đơn giản — Superpowers nhẹ hơn
Khi không dùng Claude Code

cards.name: Planning with Files
cards.desc: Markdown-file-based planning skill inspired by Manus — maintains context across multiple work sessions.
cards.detail: Planning-with-files implements a persistent planning model using 3 markdown files: task_plan.md (goals + phases), findings.md (discovery notes), progress.md (progress log). Follows the '2-Action Rule' — after every 2 view/search actions, findings must be recorded. Includes hooks that auto-read task_plan before every write action to prevent drifting from original goals. Inspired by the Manus workflow (acquired by Meta for $2B). Supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor.
whenToUse: Khi cần persistent planning across sessions (survive /clear)
Khi dự án phức tạp cần structured task tracking
Khi muốn Manus-style workflow với markdown planning files
whenNotToUse: Khi dự án đơn giản không cần planning phase
Khi đã dùng Superpowers (có planning skills riêng)

cards.name: Claude-Flow
cards.desc: Agent orchestration platform with a Queen + Workers architecture — manages Claude, GPT, and Gemini simultaneously via MCP.
cards.detail: Multi-agent orchestration framework using a Queen + Workers model. Queen (Claude Opus) plans and assigns tasks to Workers (which can be Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI). Features: HNSW vector memory, swarm mode (60+ agents), multi-model routing via MCP, parallel execution. MIT license.

parallel task execution with Claude Code
complex project automation
background worker workflows
whenNotToUse: simple single-agent tasks
non-Claude environments
lightweight scripting

cards.desc: Personal AI assistant running 24/7 — chat via 15+ channels including WhatsApp, Telegram, Zalo.

cards.name: oh-my-claudecode
cards.desc: Team-based multi-agent orchestration plugin for Claude Code — staged plan → build → verify pipeline, autopilot, Codex/Gemini workers
cards.detail:
oh-my-claudecode (OMC) is an open-source (MIT) plugin and CLI that adds multi-agent orchestration on top of Claude Code. Its main surface is Team mode: a staged pipeline that plans the task, writes a spec, executes with several agents, verifies the result and loops on fixes. Autopilot runs a task end to end through configurable stages, Ralph keeps working until the result is verified, and Deep Interview clarifies vague requirements before any code is written. From the terminal, `omc team` can start tmux worker panes running Claude, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity or Cursor CLIs, and `omc ask` routes a question to another provider. Install it from the Claude Code plugin marketplace or via npm; it needs a working Claude Code setup. Compared with Ruflo (formerly Claude-Flow), which is a broader swarm and memory harness, OMC focuses on phase-by-phase team workflows inside Claude Code.

Works well with: Claude Code · Codex CLI · Gemini CLI · tmux
whenToUse: You use Claude Code and want a team of agents to plan, build and verify a task in stages
You want to hand a task to autopilot and get back verified work
You want Codex or Gemini CLI workers alongside Claude in one workflow
whenNotToUse: You do not use Claude Code (the Codex edition is a separate project)
You want a broad swarm/memory platform across many agents — see Ruflo (Claude-Flow)
You need a VS Code extension or a hosted service — OMC is a plugin and terminal CLI

sections.title: AI Coding Agents — AI-Powered Coding Tools

cards.name: Claude Code
cards.desc: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for terminal, IDE, desktop and web — reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, opens PRs.
cards.detail: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. It reads your codebase, edits multiple files, runs commands and tests, and works with git — staging changes, writing commits and opening pull requests. It is available as a CLI, VS Code/Cursor and JetBrains extensions, a desktop app and on the web (claude.ai/code), where long tasks run in the cloud; sessions can move between surfaces (for example with claude --teleport). Customize it with CLAUDE.md (or an existing AGENTS.md), skills, hooks, MCP servers, subagents and plugins; the Agent SDK builds custom agents on the same engine, and GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD run it in pipelines. Claude models only — through a paid Claude plan, the Anthropic API, or cloud providers such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud. Best for: complex multi-file work, large refactors and existing codebases.
whenToUse: Agentic coding from the terminal or IDE on real, existing codebases
Multi-file refactoring and changes that need whole-repo awareness
Delegating long tasks to run in the cloud while you do something else
whenNotToUse: You want to use non-Claude models (OpenCode, Cline or goose are provider-agnostic)
You mainly need inline tab completion in the IDE (Copilot or Cursor)
No paid Claude plan or API budget — Claude Code is not included in the free plan

cards.name: Cursor
cards.desc: AI-first code editor built on VS Code — Agent, Tab predictions, a CLI and parallel cloud agents.
cards.detail: Cursor is an AI code editor forked from VS Code. Agent edits across files and runs terminal commands, Tab predicts your next edit, and Inline Edit rewrites a selection. Beyond the desktop IDE there is a CLI (also headless for CI), cloud agents that work in parallel in their own environments, Bugbot for pull-request review, and JetBrains support via ACP. Extensible with Rules, MCP servers, skills, subagents and hooks. Models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI plus Cursor's own Composer model; on current plans, third-party model usage is billed separately at API prices. Cursor was acquired by SpaceX in August 2026. Best for: daily coding and multi-file changes inside one AI-native editor.
whenToUse: You want agent, tab completion and codebase context in one AI-native IDE
Multi-file edits and refactoring driven from the editor
You want several agents working in parallel in the cloud, then review their PRs
whenNotToUse: You want to keep your current editor — Cursor is a separate IDE (JetBrains only via ACP)
You need predictable spend — third-party model usage is billed on top of the plan

cards.name: Codex CLI
cards.desc: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for the terminal — works on your local repo inside an OS sandbox; part of the Codex family with IDE, desktop and cloud.
cards.detail: Codex CLI is OpenAI's open-source (Apache-2.0) coding agent, written in Rust. It works on your local repository — inspecting files, editing code and running commands inside a local OS-level sandbox, with approval modes that decide when it may edit or execute without asking. Project instructions live in AGENTS.md (create one with /init); MCP servers, skills and plugins extend it, and codex exec runs it non-interactively in scripts and CI. The wider Codex product adds an IDE extension, a desktop app and cloud tasks (codex cloud). Sign in with a ChatGPT plan, where Codex is included, or use an API key. OpenAI models by default; open models via Ollama (--oss) and custom providers are also supported.
whenToUse: You already pay for ChatGPT and want a terminal coding agent included in the plan
You want an open-source agent with a local sandbox and explicit approval modes
Scripted or CI automation with codex exec
whenNotToUse: You want an IDE-first experience with inline completions (Cursor, Copilot)
You want non-OpenAI models as a first-class option — OpenAI models are the default and best supported

cards.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
cards.desc: Cognition's AI IDE, formerly Windsurf — Devin Local agent, Tab completions, local and cloud agents in one editor.
cards.detail: Windsurf was renamed Devin Desktop in 2026 by Cognition, the team behind Devin; existing Windsurf users received it as an update with their plan unchanged. It is a standalone AI IDE for macOS, Windows and Linux that can import VS Code and Cursor settings. The main agent is now Devin Local, the successor to Cascade (legacy Cascade remained available until 1 July 2026), sharing its harness with Devin CLI. An Agent Command Center manages local agents and Devin Cloud agents, and ACP-compatible agents such as Codex or Claude Agent can run inside it. Also: Tab completions, Workflows, Memories, Rules, MCP, in-editor preview and app deploys. The Windsurf JetBrains plugin is in maintenance mode; JetBrains users are pointed to Devin over ACP.

sources.title: Cognition — Windsurf is now Devin Desktop

whenToUse: You want a standalone AI IDE that runs local agents and can hand work to cloud agents (Devin)
Moving from VS Code or Cursor — settings can be imported
You want to drive several agents (Devin Local, Codex, Claude Agent via ACP) from one editor
whenNotToUse: You work in JetBrains IDEs — the Windsurf plugin is in maintenance mode
You depend on specific VS Code extensions — the extension marketplace is restricted
You need settled pricing — plans are still in transition after the rename

cards.name: GitHub Copilot
cards.desc: GitHub's AI coding assistant — IDE extensions with agent mode, a cloud agent that works from issues, Copilot CLI and PR review.
cards.detail: GitHub Copilot works inside VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, Eclipse and Neovim with code completions, chat and agent mode (generally available). The cloud agent picks up assigned issues, works in the background and opens pull requests; Copilot code review comments on PRs; Copilot CLI brings the agent to the terminal with MCP, hooks, skills and custom agents. Paid plans can choose models from Anthropic, OpenAI and others; Free uses automatic model selection. Since June 2026 usage is measured in GitHub AI credits, while code completions stay unlimited on paid plans. Biggest advantage: deep integration with GitHub repos, issues, PRs and Actions, plus enterprise admin, policy and MCP allow-list controls.
whenToUse: You want AI help inside your existing IDE (VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Xcode…) without switching editors
Your team lives on GitHub and wants agents that start from issues and open PRs
Organizations needing central admin, policies and MCP allow-lists
whenNotToUse: You want a dedicated AI-native IDE experience (Cursor, Devin Desktop)
Heavy agent use with a fixed budget — chat and agent usage consume AI credits
You need offline or self-hosted inference — Copilot runs in GitHub's cloud

cards.name: Gemini CLI
cards.desc: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini models — MCP, extensions, skills. Since June 2026 it needs a paid API key or Code Assist license.
cards.detail: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source (Apache-2.0) AI agent for the terminal, written in TypeScript. It reads and edits local files, runs shell commands and fetches web content, and is extended with MCP servers, extensions, agent skills, hooks and GEMINI.md context files; Gemini models offer a very large context window for reading big codebases. Access changed in 2026: on 18 June 2026 Google stopped serving Gemini CLI for Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers and for free Gemini Code Assist for individuals, moving them to the new Antigravity CLI. Gemini CLI remains available with paid Gemini API keys and with Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licenses. Best for: organizations already on Gemini Code Assist or the paid Gemini API that want an open-source CLI agent.

sources.title: Google — Transitioning Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI

whenToUse: Your organization has a Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise license or a paid Gemini API key
You want an open-source, terminal-first agent you can inspect and extend
You want Gemini models with a very large context window for big codebases
whenNotToUse: You want a free personal coding agent — free individual access ended in June 2026 (Google points to Antigravity CLI)
You need tab completion or inline suggestions in an IDE
You want models from other providers (Gemini models only)

cards.name: Cline
cards.desc: Open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal — Plan/Act modes, MCP, any model provider including local models.
cards.detail: Cline is an open-source (Apache-2.0) autonomous coding agent available as a VS Code extension, a JetBrains plugin, a CLI (interactive or headless for CI) and an SDK. Plan mode proposes a strategy and Act mode carries it out with per-action approval or optional auto-approve; checkpoints let you undo the agent's edits. Supports MCP servers and providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, Bedrock and any OpenAI-compatible API, plus local models via Ollama or LM Studio. Bring your own API key with no subscription, or use Cline's own usage billing; an Enterprise tier adds SSO and RBAC. Note: this card previously also covered Roo Code, a Cline fork — Roo Code was shut down and its repository archived on 15 May 2026.
whenToUse: You want to control API cost and pick any model, including local ones
You want an autonomous agent with step-by-step approval inside VS Code or JetBrains
You want to keep your current IDE instead of switching editors
whenNotToUse: You mainly want fast inline tab completion (Copilot or Cursor fit better)
You don't want to manage model choice and usage costs yourself

cards.name: Kiro (AWS)
cards.desc: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE and CLI — turns requirements into design, tasks and code, guided by steering files and hooks.
cards.detail: Kiro is an agentic development platform built and operated by AWS, generally available since November 2025. Its core idea is spec-driven development: write requirements, let Kiro produce a design and a task list, then implement and test them (including property-based tests). Steering files keep the agent on your project conventions; hooks run actions on file changes, tool use or task completion; MCP, Powers, skills and parallel subagents extend it. Available as an IDE (based on Code OSS), the Kiro CLI (successor to the Amazon Q Developer CLI) and Kiro Web with cloud sandboxes, all sharing the same .kiro/ configuration. Models from Anthropic, OpenAI and open-weight families with an Auto selector, billed in credits. No AWS account is required — sign in with AWS Builder ID or a social login. Best for: teams who want structured, spec-first work rather than ad-hoc prompting.
whenToUse: Spec-driven development — clear requirements and design before code
Teams coming from Amazon Q Developer — the Kiro CLI is its successor
Automating docs, tests and checks through agent hooks
whenNotToUse: Quick prototypes — the spec workflow adds overhead for small tasks
You need predictable spend — complex requests consume more credits
You prefer not to depend on an AWS-operated service

cards.name: Replit Agent
cards.desc: Browser-based agent that builds and publishes full-stack apps from a prompt — no local setup. Best for beginners and fast prototypes.
cards.detail: Replit Agent (Agent 4 since March 2026) runs inside Replit's cloud workspace: describe what you want and it plans, builds, tests and publishes web and mobile apps, dashboards and more. Plan mode and a design canvas come before code; checkpoints let you roll back; built-in auth, database, hosting and monitoring remove setup work. Connectors link services such as Slack, Notion, Linear and BigQuery. Agent usage is effort-based (billed per checkpoint against monthly credits), so cost depends on the size of each task. Best for: rapid prototyping, learning to code and internal tools when you don't want a local dev environment.
whenToUse: Turn an idea into a working, hosted web app from a natural-language description
Prototype without setting up a local environment
You want auth, database and hosting bundled with the build
whenNotToUse: Projects needing tight cost control — effort-based agent pricing varies by task
You need to work offline or on your own machine or infrastructure

cards.name: OpenCode
cards.desc: Open-source coding agent with a terminal UI, desktop app and IDE extension — works with almost any model provider or local models. MIT license.
cards.detail: OpenCode is an open-source (MIT) coding agent built by Anomaly, the team behind SST; the repository now lives at anomalyco/opencode. It is written in TypeScript with its own OpenTUI terminal interface, and is also available as a desktop app (beta), an IDE extension, a web UI and a GitHub/GitLab integration. Two built-in agents — build (full access) and plan (read-only) — are switched with Tab, plus subagents for side tasks. It connects to many providers through Models.dev, can sign in with GitHub Copilot or ChatGPT plans, and supports local models; LSP servers load automatically for code intelligence. Extensible with MCP servers, plugins, custom agents, skills and tools. Free with your own keys; optional paid hosted models (Zen, Go).
whenToUse: You want an open-source, provider-agnostic alternative to Claude Code or Codex CLI
You like a terminal-first workflow with a polished TUI
You want plan/build agent switching — analyze before editing
whenNotToUse: You prefer a full IDE experience — the desktop app is still in beta
You don't want to set up model providers yourself
You need long-term stability of commands and config — the project changes very fast

cards.name: Goose
cards.desc: Open-source local AI agent with desktop app and CLI — runs commands, edits code and automates workflows with any LLM. Now under the Linux Foundation.
cards.detail: goose is an open-source (Apache-2.0) general-purpose AI agent created by Block and contributed in December 2025 to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation, alongside MCP and AGENTS.md; the repository is now aaif-goose/goose and the docs moved to goose-docs.ai. Written in Rust, it runs on your machine as a desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows), a CLI or an embeddable API. It executes commands, installs dependencies and debugs rather than only suggesting code, and is also used for research, writing and data tasks. Extensible with MCP extensions; Recipes are portable YAML workflows that can be shared and run in CI. Works with many providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, Bedrock…), existing subscriptions via ACP, or fully local models through Ollama.
whenToUse: You need an LLM-agnostic agent that works with any provider
You want to automate repeatable workflows with shareable YAML recipes
Data privacy matters — run fully local with Ollama
whenNotToUse: You want zero setup — you must configure a model provider first
You want top coding accuracy out of the box without tuning the model choice

sections.title: AI Trends 2026 — Trends Shaping the Future

cards.name: Multi-Agent Systems
cards.desc: Multi-agent AI systems working in coordination — Gartner reports 1,445% surge in interest. 40% of enterprise apps will use agents by late 2026.
cards.detail: Gartner reports queries about multi-agent systems surged 1,445% from Q1/2024 to Q2/2025. Predicted 40% of enterprise apps will integrate AI agents by late 2026 (vs 5% in 2025). By 2027, 70% of MAS will use specialized agents instead of general-purpose ones. Agentic AI market from $7.8B (2025) to $52B (2030). Trend: from monolithic agents to orchestrated teams — similar to the microservices revolution.

sources.title: Gartner — 40% Enterprise Apps with AI Agents by 2026
Gartner — Multiagent Systems in Enterprise AI

Tự động hóa quy trình end-to-end thay vì từng task riêng lẻ
Khi team/org cần agents phối hợp cross-functional
whenNotToUse: Task đơn giản chỉ cần 1 agent hoặc 1 LLM call
Chưa có observability/governance cho hệ thống phân tán
Prototype nhanh — overhead orchestration chưa cần thiết

cards.name: Mechanistic Interpretability
cards.desc: Research into how AI 'thinks' internally — enabling better understanding and control of AI behavior. 2026 breakthrough per MIT.
cards.detail: MIT Technology Review selected this as one of the 10 Breakthrough Technologies of 2026. Anthropic used an 'AI microscope' to discover 34 million features in Claude — from 'sarcasm' to 'DNA sequences'. OpenAI built an 'AI lie detector' based on model internals. Google DeepMind released Gemma Scope 2 — the largest open-source interpretability toolkit. Goal: turning AI from a 'black box' into a 'glass box' — understanding why AI makes its decisions.

sources.title: MIT Tech Review — LLMs like alien autopsy

Nghiên cứu AI safety, alignment, phát hiện deception
Audit model trước khi deploy cho ứng dụng high-stakes

Không có background ML/deep learning chuyên sâu
Cần giải pháp production nhanh, không phải research

cards.name: World Models
cards.desc: AI simulating the real world — AMI Labs, Google, and startups are racing to develop it. Gaming is a major driver.
cards.detail: AI simulating the real world — LeCun left Meta to cofound AMI Labs, while Google and startups are racing to develop it. World models understand physics, predict outcomes of actions in 3D environments. Applications: autonomous driving, robotics, game development, simulation. Gaming is a major driver. Recent: Genie 2 (Google), video generation models becoming world simulators.

sources.title: Yann LeCun — A Path Towards Autonomous AI

whenToUse: Xây dựng AI hiểu vật lý và spatial reasoning cho robotics
Training agents trong simulated environments trước khi deploy thực tế
Tạo interactive 3D environments cho gaming hoặc VR/AR
whenNotToUse: Chỉ cần text processing hoặc chatbot thông thường
Không có GPU infrastructure đủ mạnh
Dự án không liên quan đến spatial/physical reasoning

cards.name: Generative Coding
cards.desc: AI writes 30% of code at Microsoft, 25%+ at Google. 'English is becoming the new programming language.'
cards.detail: AI writes 30% of code at Microsoft, 25%+ at Google. GitHub Copilot has ~30% suggestion acceptance rate. MIT Technology Review selected this as a 2026 Breakthrough. However, Veracode found 45% of AI-generated code contains security vulnerabilities. Trend: 'English is becoming the new programming language' — developers shifting from writing code to guiding AI to write code.

Non-developers cần build apps/prototypes nhanh (vibe coding)
Cần generate, test, debug code tự động trong pipeline
whenNotToUse: Security-critical code không có human review process
Codebase legacy phức tạp cần deep architectural understanding
Cần 100% deterministic, auditable code output

cards.name: Chinese Open-Source AI
cards.desc: DeepSeek R1 shook the AI world — open-source reasoning model from China. Technology gap shrinking from months to weeks.
cards.detail: DeepSeek R1 caused shockwaves — open-source reasoning model from China, performance near GPT-4 at much lower cost. Qwen (Alibaba) continuously updated, competing directly with frontier models. US-China technology gap shrinking from months to weeks. Trend: China is no longer just 'copying' but 'innovating' — especially in efficiency and cost optimization.

Fine-tune cho use case riêng
Self-host LLM để kiểm soát dữ liệu
Xây prototype nhanh với model mở

Quy định nghiêm ngặt về nguồn gốc model
Không có hạ tầng GPU để chạy local

cards.name: Post-Training > Pre-Training
cards.desc: Trend toward post-training refinement instead of building larger models — RL and fine-tuning become the key.
cards.detail: Major trend: instead of training larger models (pre-training costs $100M+), focus shifts to post-training refinement using RLHF, DPO, RLAIF. Fine-tuning becomes the key — small models + good fine-tuning can beat larger models. Reasoning models (o1, o3, DeepSeek R1) prove post-training matters more than model size.

Tăng reasoning qua reinforcement learning
Cải thiện model chi phí thấp hơn pre-training
Fine-tune cho domain chuyên biệt
whenNotToUse: Chưa có base model đủ mạnh
Không có preference data hoặc verifiable rewards
Task đơn giản dùng prompt engineering là đủ

cards.name: AI Drug Discovery
cards.desc: AI-discovered drugs entering mid/late-stage clinical trials. Focus: cancer and rare diseases.
cards.detail: AI accelerating new drug discovery — from 10-15 years down to 2-3 years for the discovery phase. AlphaFold predicts protein structures, Isomorphic Labs (Google) partnering with Eli Lilly and Novartis. Insilico Medicine advancing AI-designed drugs to Phase II clinical trials. Focus: cancer, rare diseases, new antibiotics.

Thiết kế phân tử thuốc mới
Sàng lọc ứng viên thuốc quy mô lớn
Tối ưu thuộc tính dược lý bằng AI
whenNotToUse: Không có dữ liệu sinh học chuyên ngành
Cần kết quả lâm sàng ngay lập tức
Không có hạ tầng tính toán hiệu năng cao

cards.name: AI Infrastructure
cards.desc: Massive 1GW+ data centers, even using nuclear power for AI. A core battleground in the AI race.
cards.detail: Massive 1GW+ data centers being built — even using nuclear power. Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are pursuing long-term nuclear energy deals. AI infrastructure investment is accelerating rapidly. NVIDIA H100/H200 supply remains a key bottleneck.

Tối ưu chi phí GPU và compute
Xây hạ tầng inference gần người dùng
Quản lý cluster training phân tán

Prototype nhỏ không cần scale
Không có ngân sách hạ tầng chuyên dụng

cards.name: AI Governance
cards.desc: AI agents monitoring other AI agents — setting safety guardrails and keeping humans in the loop.
cards.detail: AI agents monitoring other AI agents — 'governance agents' detecting policy violations. EU AI Act fully effective in 2026. Gartner predicts 2,000+ 'death by AI' lawsuits by late 2026 due to missing guardrails. 'Bounded autonomy' — agents with clear action limits, escalation paths when uncertain. Trend: compliance-by-design instead of compliance-as-afterthought.
whenToUse: Tuân thủ EU AI Act hoặc quy định AI
Đánh giá rủi ro hệ thống AI
Xây dựng quy trình AI có trách nhiệm
Kiểm soát bias và fairness trong model
whenNotToUse: Prototype giai đoạn rất sớm
AI chỉ dùng nội bộ không ảnh hưởng end-user
Không hoạt động trong thị trường có quy định

cards.name: Langfuse
cards.desc: Open-source observability platform for LLM apps — tracing, evals, prompt management
cards.detail:
Langfuse is an open-source LLM engineering platform for teams running LLM apps in production. It records traces built on OpenTelemetry (inputs, outputs, tool calls, latency, cost), runs automated and human evaluations, manages prompts with versioning, and provides a playground and datasets for experiments. SDKs for Python and TypeScript plus integrations with common frameworks and gateways (LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI SDK, LiteLLM, Dify and more). Self-host it with Docker or Kubernetes, or use Langfuse Cloud. ClickHouse acquired Langfuse in early 2026; the team says it stays open source and self-hostable with no planned licence changes. The core is MIT; enterprise features live in separate ee/ directories under their own licence. Use it when you need end-to-end monitoring and evaluation of production LLM apps.

Works well with: LiteLLM (gateway traces) · LangGraph · LlamaIndex · Dify · vLLM
whenToUse: You need to trace LLM calls, latency and cost in production
You want versioned prompt management shared by the team
You need to evaluate LLM output quality with automated and human scoring
whenNotToUse: You only need simple offline evals without tracing
Your project does not use LLMs

cards.name: DeepEval
cards.desc: Open-source LLM evaluation framework in the style of Pytest — research-based metrics, agent and multi-turn evals, CI/CD
cards.detail:
DeepEval is "Pytest for LLMs": you write test cases for LLM outputs and assert on metrics such as G-Eval, hallucination, faithfulness, answer relevancy and contextual precision/recall for RAG. It also covers agentic evals (tool use, task completion) and multi-turn conversations, generates synthetic test data, and runs in CI/CD to catch regressions. Python is the main SDK, and TypeScript integrations exist for frameworks such as the Vercel AI SDK and Mastra. Red teaming has moved to Confident AI's companion project DeepTeam. Confident AI is the optional hosted platform for dashboards, datasets and tracing. Use it when you want evaluation to be part of your test suite.

Works well with: LangGraph · LlamaIndex · RAG pipelines · CI (GitHub Actions)
whenToUse: You want to unit-test LLM output in CI/CD
You need to evaluate a RAG pipeline or an agent
You want research-backed metrics without building your own eval harness
whenNotToUse: You need a full production observability platform
You mainly need red teaming (use its companion project DeepTeam or Promptfoo)

cards.name: Promptfoo
cards.desc: Open-source CLI for prompt testing, model comparison and LLM red teaming / security scanning
cards.detail:
Promptfoo is an open-source (MIT) CLI and library for testing and securing LLM apps. You describe prompts, providers and assertions in YAML, then compare outputs side by side across models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, local models via Ollama) and catch regressions. Its red-teaming module probes apps for issues such as prompt injection, jailbreaks and PII leaks, and it runs in CI/CD, for example through GitHub Actions. OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire Promptfoo in March 2026; the team says the open-source tools will remain open source. An enterprise edition adds team features and managed options. Ideal for teams that want a security-first testing workflow.

Works well with: Ollama · LiteLLM · GitHub Actions · Any LLM provider
whenToUse: You want to compare outputs across LLMs
You need to catch prompt regressions before release
You want red teaming and security scans for an LLM app
whenNotToUse: You need real-time production observability
You need distributed tracing across services

cards.name: LangSmith
cards.desc: Observability and evaluation platform from the LangChain team — tracing, evals, prompt hub; works with any framework
cards.detail:
LangSmith is the LangChain team's platform for observing, evaluating and improving LLM apps and agents. It traces every step (inputs, outputs, tool calls, intermediate decisions), runs automated and human evaluations with annotation queues, and manages prompts with versioning and a playground for cross-model testing. Integration with LangChain and LangGraph is deepest, but tracing is framework-agnostic: it works with the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, the Vercel AI SDK, LlamaIndex or custom code, and can ingest OpenTelemetry data. Available as managed cloud with a free tier, bring-your-own-cloud, or self-hosted for Enterprise. A natural default if you already build with LangChain or LangGraph.

Works well with: LangGraph · LlamaIndex · LiteLLM · OpenTelemetry
whenToUse: Debugging LangChain and LangGraph applications
Tracing agent execution step by step
Evaluating quality with datasets and annotation queues
whenNotToUse: You need a fully free, self-hosted tool (self-hosting is an Enterprise option)
You need an open-source tool you can modify

cards.name: Arize Phoenix
cards.desc: Open-source AI observability platform — tracing, evaluation, prompt management, RAG debugging
cards.detail:
Arize Phoenix is an open-source observability platform for experimenting with and troubleshooting LLM apps. Built on OpenTelemetry (OpenInference instrumentation), it is vendor-agnostic and traces apps built with LlamaIndex, LangChain, DSPy, smolagents, the OpenAI SDK and more. It runs LLM-as-judge and code-based evaluations, datasets and experiments, and prompt management with versioning and a playground; inference analysis with embedding visualisation helps debug retrieval in RAG apps. Run it locally, in a notebook, or self-host it with Docker or Kubernetes. Licensed under Elastic License 2.0 (source-available: free to use and self-host, but not to offer as a managed service); Arize AX is the company's separate commercial platform. Good fit for research teams and RAG-heavy applications.

Works well with: LlamaIndex · LangGraph · LiteLLM · OpenTelemetry
whenToUse: Debugging RAG retrieval quality
Analysing traces with OpenTelemetry instrumentation
Running evaluations inside notebook workflows
whenNotToUse: You want to offer it to third parties as a managed service (Elastic License 2.0 forbids this)
You need an OSI-approved permissive licence

cards.name: Ollama
cards.desc: The simplest way to run open LLMs on your own machine — a few commands to start, OpenAI-compatible API
cards.detail:
Ollama runs open models such as Llama, DeepSeek, Gemma, Qwen and Mistral on your own machine with minimal setup: install it (a script on macOS/Linux, an installer on Windows), pull a model and run it. It manages model downloads, quantised formats and GPU/CPU use for you, and exposes a local API that is compatible with the OpenAI format. Runs on macOS, Linux and Windows. Running models locally is free and unlimited; since 2025 Ollama also offers cloud models for larger models, with paid plans that add usage credits. Perfect for developers who want to experiment with LLMs locally without API costs, or prototype before moving to a serving stack.

Works well with: LiteLLM (gateway) · Dify · Open-source RAG tools · Promptfoo (local model tests)
whenToUse: Running LLMs on a local machine without a GPU server
Prototyping quickly with open models without an API key
whenNotToUse: You need production-scale, high-throughput serving (see vLLM)
You need models that require a multi-GPU cluster

cards.name: vLLM
cards.desc: High-throughput inference and serving engine for LLMs in production — PagedAttention, continuous batching
cards.detail:
vLLM is an open-source (Apache 2.0) engine for serving LLMs at high throughput. PagedAttention manages GPU memory for the KV cache efficiently, and continuous batching keeps hardware busy under many concurrent requests. It supports tensor and pipeline parallelism, speculative decoding, quantisation and prefix caching, and serves an OpenAI-compatible API server. It runs on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs and other accelerators, with CPU support for x86, ARM and PowerPC, and covers most popular open model architectures (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek and more). vLLM has been hosted by the PyTorch Foundation since May 2025. Use it when you need to serve open models to many users.

Works well with: LiteLLM (gateway in front of vLLM) · Langfuse (tracing) · Kubernetes
whenToUse: You need high-throughput LLM serving in production
You want to make the most of GPU memory and concurrency
whenNotToUse: You just want to run a model on a laptop (Ollama is simpler)
You have no GPU or accelerator and need fast responses (CPU support is slower)

cards.name: LocalAI
cards.desc: Self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible AI server — run LLMs, image, audio and video models on your own hardware, GPU optional
cards.detail:
LocalAI is a self-hosted drop-in replacement for the OpenAI API that runs on your own hardware, with no GPU required (GPUs are used when available). One server covers text generation, embeddings, image and video generation, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and vision, all behind OpenAI-compatible endpoints; it also speaks the Anthropic and ElevenLabs API formats and the Responses API, and can run agents that use MCP tools. Deploy it with a single Docker command or a binary. MIT licensed. Ideal for teams that want to keep their whole AI stack and data in-house.

Works well with: MCP (agent tools) · Dify (as a model provider) · Docker/Kubernetes
whenToUse: You need a drop-in replacement for the OpenAI API on your own infrastructure
You want one server for several model types (text, image, audio, video)
whenNotToUse: You only need to run one model simply — Ollama is simpler
You need maximum serving throughput — vLLM fits better

cards.name: LiteLLM
cards.desc: Open-source AI gateway and SDK for many LLM providers — one API, cost tracking, load balancing, fallbacks
cards.detail:
LiteLLM gives you one OpenAI-style API for many LLM providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Ollama, vLLM and more. Use it as a Python SDK or run the proxy server (AI gateway) so any language can call it. The gateway tracks cost per request, user and key, enforces budgets and rate limits, load-balances across deployments and falls back automatically when a provider fails; it sends logs and traces to tools such as Langfuse and LangSmith. A Rust-based gateway is in beta (since mid-2026). The code is MIT apart from an enterprise/ directory under a separate commercial licence (enterprise features need a licence key). Ideal for teams using several LLM providers who want central control of keys and spend.

Works well with: Ollama · vLLM · Langfuse · LangSmith
whenToUse: You need to call many LLM APIs through one interface
You need cost tracking, rate limits and load balancing across models
whenNotToUse: You only use a single LLM provider
You do not need a proxy layer — calling the API directly is enough

cards.name: Dify
cards.desc: Open-source platform for building AI apps and agents with a visual workflow builder and built-in RAG pipeline
cards.detail:
Dify is an all-in-one platform for building AI applications, from chatbots to agents, with little code. Its core is a drag-and-drop visual workflow builder: connect nodes (LLM, knowledge retrieval, tools, logic) into a complete flow and publish it as an app or API. The built-in RAG pipeline handles upload, chunking, embedding and retrieval with hybrid search and reranking; the default Docker Compose stack bundles a vector store (Weaviate), and you can switch to Milvus, Qdrant, pgvector, Chroma and others. Agents can call Marketplace tools and MCP servers and run commands in their own sandbox. Model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) are installed as plugins. LLMOps logs and annotations are built in, with tracing integrations such as Langfuse, Opik and Arize Phoenix. Run it with Docker Compose, use Dify Cloud, or use Dify Enterprise for self-hosted organisations. Real-world use cases: internal knowledge-base chatbots, customer-support assistants, document-processing workflows, and prototyping AI app ideas before building custom code. Note: the Dify Open Source License is Apache 2.0 plus conditions — running a multi-tenant service needs written permission and the frontend logo and copyright must stay — check it before commercial use.

Works well with: Ollama (local LLM) · Langfuse (observability) · Milvus/Qdrant/pgvector (replace the default vector store) · LiteLLM (model gateway) · MCP (tool access)
whenToUse: You need a visual workflow builder for RAG apps and AI agents
You want to take an LLM app from prototype to production quickly (self-host or Dify Cloud)
Your team wants RAG, model management, agents and LLMOps in one platform
whenNotToUse: You need a pure OSI license for a multi-tenant SaaS (the Dify license requires written permission)
You only need a lightweight RAG engine, not a full platform
You want a minimal stack — the default deployment runs PostgreSQL or MySQL, Redis, Weaviate, a code sandbox and a plugin daemon

cards.name: RAGFlow
cards.desc: Open-source RAG engine built on deep document understanding — layout-aware parsing, template chunking, grounded citations
cards.detail:
RAGFlow is a RAG engine focused on document-processing quality, the step that most often decides whether answers are right. Its DeepDoc pipeline parses complex documents — tables, images, scanned PDFs, slides — with OCR and layout recognition, then chunks them by template with a visual preview so users can adjust the result. Every answer carries citations back to the source chunks, which makes hallucinations easier to spot. Beyond retrieval it offers an agent builder with tool calls, agentic retrieval with selectable reasoning depth, and knowledge compilation into wikis, graphs, mind maps and timelines. Documents are indexed in Elasticsearch by default, with Infinity as an alternative engine. Self-host it with Docker Compose (Apache 2.0) or use the official RAGFlow Cloud, which has a free plan and paid team plans. Real-world use cases: enterprise Q&A over contracts, technical reports and legal documents — documents where naive chunking gives poor answers.

Works well with: Ollama (LLM backend) · Elasticsearch/Infinity (document engine) · Dify (as an external knowledge base) · Any LLM provider (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini)
whenToUse: You need a RAG engine that handles complex documents (PDFs, tables, scans)
You want deep document understanding that you can fully self-host
You need traceable citations for every answer
whenNotToUse: You want a no-code builder for a non-technical team
You want a minimal setup — self-hosting runs Elasticsearch, MySQL, MinIO and other services and needs a well-provisioned server
You want to store vectors in a specific database such as Milvus or Qdrant (RAGFlow uses its own document engines)

cards.name: AnythingLLM
cards.desc: Local-first, all-in-one app to chat with your documents and run AI agents — desktop or multi-user Docker server
cards.detail:
AnythingLLM is an open-source (MIT) application for chatting with your own documents and running AI agents without assembling a stack yourself. Install the desktop app on macOS, Windows or Linux, or run the Docker version, which adds multi-user workspaces with permissions and an embeddable chat widget; a paid hosted instance is also offered. Documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT and more) are split into workspaces and answered with citations. By default it uses a built-in local model engine, a built-in embedder and LanceDB as the vector store, so it can run on your own machine; you can instead connect cloud LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and others), local servers such as Ollama or LM Studio, and vector databases such as PGVector, Chroma, Qdrant or Milvus — data then goes to whichever services you pick. Agents can browse the web and call MCP tools, built with a no-code flow builder. Anonymous telemetry is on by default and can be disabled.

Works well with: Ollama · LiteLLM · LocalAI · PGVector/Chroma/Qdrant/Milvus
whenToUse: You want private chat over your documents on a laptop with minimal setup
A small team needs a shared, self-hosted document assistant with user permissions
You want to try local or cloud models in one app before building a custom RAG stack
whenNotToUse: You need deep parsing of complex PDFs, tables and scans — see RAGFlow
You want to design multi-step AI workflows and publish them as apps or APIs — see Dify
You need graph-based retrieval across entities — see LightRAG

cards.name: LightRAG
cards.desc: Lightweight graph-based RAG framework — builds a knowledge graph from documents (HKU research, Findings of EMNLP 2025)
cards.detail:
LightRAG takes a different approach from plain vector RAG: it uses an LLM to extract entities and the relationships between them from documents, builds a knowledge graph, and combines graph traversal with vector retrieval at local and global levels when answering. It comes from research at the University of Hong Kong; the paper, published in Findings of EMNLP 2025, reports better results than several baseline RAG methods. Use it as a Python library or run LightRAG Server, which provides a REST API and a web UI for managing documents and querying the graph. Storage is pluggable: in-memory defaults for testing, and PostgreSQL (recommended for production), Neo4j, Memgraph, MongoDB, OpenSearch, Milvus or Qdrant for real workloads. Practical applications: knowledge management, research Q&A that depends on relationships between concepts, or any problem where 'who is related to what' matters more than 'which chunks are similar'.

Works well with: Ollama (local LLM) · PostgreSQL/pgvector (production storage) · Neo4j (graph storage) · LlamaIndex (see Agent Frameworks)
whenToUse: You need graph-based RAG with a knowledge graph built automatically from documents
You want a lightweight engine you can embed in Python or call over a REST API
You are comparing graph RAG with vector RAG in research or a prototype
whenNotToUse: You need a full team platform with an app builder, user management and monitoring
Your team is not ready to tune entity extraction and knowledge-graph quality
You need low indexing cost — building the graph calls the LLM for every document

cards.name: Milvus
cards.desc: Open-source, cloud-native vector database for large-scale search — a graduated LF AI & Data Foundation project
cards.detail:
Milvus is a vector database designed for scale: it runs as an embedded library (Milvus Lite), a single Docker container, or a distributed cluster on Kubernetes that scales horizontally to billions of vectors. It supports many index types (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN and quantized variants), dense and sparse vectors, full-text (BM25) and hybrid search, and metadata filtering, so you can trade off speed, recall and cost per workload. Its 2026 major release went 'lake-native': Milvus can query data kept in external Parquet, Lance, Iceberg or Vortex files in place, add or drop fields online, and take snapshots. Milvus is a graduated project of the LF AI & Data Foundation; Zilliz offers it as a managed service (Zilliz Cloud, with a free tier). Practical applications: large-scale recommendation, image and video similarity search, semantic search over millions of documents, and multi-tenant RAG backends.

Works well with: LlamaIndex · Dify · LightRAG · LangChain · Any embedding model (OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face)
whenToUse: Vector search at very large scale (billions of vectors)
Hybrid search combining keyword (BM25) and semantic retrieval
Multi-tenant production workloads with strict performance needs
whenNotToUse: A small prototype that needs the simplest possible setup
You already run PostgreSQL and only need basic vector search

cards.name: Qdrant
cards.desc: Vector database written in Rust — fast, memory-efficient, with rich payload filtering built into search
cards.detail:
Qdrant (pronounced 'quadrant') is a vector database built for production performance, written in Rust. Its standout feature is filtering: it combines vector similarity with conditions on payload metadata (boolean logic, ranges, geo, full-text, nested objects) inside the search itself rather than filtering afterwards, so results stay accurate. It supports dense, sparse and multi-vector search, hybrid queries and quantization to reduce memory use, with REST and gRPC APIs and official SDKs for several languages. Run it with Docker or Kubernetes, use Qdrant Cloud (free tier available), or Qdrant Hybrid Cloud to keep clusters in your own infrastructure. Practical applications: personalised recommendations, e-commerce search that combines semantics with price and category filters, and multi-tenant RAG that needs isolation between tenants.

Works well with: LangChain · LangGraph · LlamaIndex · Dify · LightRAG · Docker/Kubernetes
whenToUse: High-performance vector search on a Rust engine
Similarity search combined with complex metadata filters
Recommendation and semantic search applications
whenNotToUse: You want vectors inside your existing PostgreSQL database
You only need a simple embedded vector store

cards.name: Chroma
cards.desc: Open-source search infrastructure for AI apps — starts embedded with zero config, adds full-text and hybrid search
cards.detail:
Chroma is an open-source (Apache 2.0) database for AI search with a developer-first API: pip install it and run it embedded in your Python process, or start it as a server. You add documents, query in natural language and get back the most similar results; Chroma can embed text with built-in models or take your own embeddings. Beyond vector search it supports metadata filtering, full-text search including regex, sparse retrieval (BM25, SPLADE) and hybrid queries. The docs describe three modes: local (embedded, for prototyping), single-node (one server for modest workloads) and distributed — offered as Chroma Cloud, a usage-based managed service with free starter credits, or as BYOC. SDKs exist for Python, TypeScript and Rust. Best suited for prototypes, side projects and small-to-medium apps, with a managed path when you need to scale.

Works well with: LangChain · LlamaIndex · CrewAI (default knowledge store) · Dify · OpenAI embeddings · Hugging Face models
whenToUse: Prototyping RAG quickly with a simple API
An embedded vector store inside a Python app
Developers who want a zero-config start
whenNotToUse: You want to self-host a distributed, highly available cluster (distributed Chroma comes as Chroma Cloud or BYOC)
Very large production workloads on your own infrastructure

cards.name: pgvector
cards.desc: Extension that turns PostgreSQL into a vector database — no separate DB needed, uses familiar SQL
cards.detail:
pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension that adds vector storage and similarity search to the relational database you already run. Instead of deploying a separate vector database, you add a vector column to existing tables and query it with SQL. It supports exact and approximate search (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes), several vector types (single and half precision, binary and sparse), and distance metrics including L2, cosine, inner product, L1, Hamming and Jaccard. Iterative index scans keep filtered queries accurate when a WHERE clause removes many candidates. It is available on most managed Postgres services, including Supabase, Neon and Amazon RDS. Practical applications: adding semantic search to a web app that already uses Postgres, simple RAG pipelines without extra infrastructure, or queries that JOIN vectors with relational data (users, orders, products).

Works well with: PostgreSQL/Supabase · LangChain · LlamaIndex · Dify · LightRAG · pgvectorscale (TigerData, performance add-on)
whenToUse: You already use PostgreSQL and need vector search
You need ACID transactions and JOINs with relational data
You do not want to run a separate database for vectors
whenNotToUse: Vector search over billions of vectors
You do not use PostgreSQL

cards.name: garak
cards.desc: LLM vulnerability scanner – probes security flaws in AI models
cards.detail:
garak is the "nmap for LLMs" – a vulnerability scanner built specifically for large language models, developed by NVIDIA. Tests for hallucination, data leakage, prompt injection, jailbreak, toxicity generation and many other attack vectors. garak operates on a modular architecture with probes (generate test interactions), detectors (identify bad behavior), and evaluators (assess results). Supports scanning models from Hugging Face, OpenAI, Ollama, LiteLLM and virtually any REST endpoint.

Works well with: NeMo Guardrails · Ollama · LiteLLM · Promptfoo
whenToUse: LLM security assessment and vulnerability scanning before deployment
red-teaming LLM applications for jailbreaks and prompt injection
automated probe-based testing across multiple failure modes
CI/CD integration for ongoing LLM security regression testing
whenNotToUse: runtime protection or guardrails (use NeMo Guardrails or Guardrails AI)
non-LLM application security testing
when need real-time blocking rather than assessment reports

cards.name: NeMo Guardrails
cards.desc: Programmable guardrails for LLMs with Colang DSL – dialog control and safety
cards.detail:
NeMo Guardrails is an open-source toolkit from NVIDIA for adding programmable guardrails to LLM applications. Uses Colang – a custom DSL for defining conversation flows, topic control, fact-checking and jailbreak prevention. Supports input/output rails, dialog rails, and retrieval rails. Integrates natively with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and NVIDIA NIM microservices for content safety and topic control. Especially suited for enterprise AI requiring strict control over interaction flows.

Works well with: garak · LangGraph · LlamaIndex · Ollama
whenToUse: topic control and content filtering for LLM chatbots
jailbreak detection in production conversational agents
multi-rail orchestration with configurable policies
dialog flow control with Colang DSL
whenNotToUse: non-conversational LLM use cases (batch processing, code gen)
when minimal added latency is critical
simple output format validation only (Guardrails AI may suffice)

cards.name: Presidio
cards.desc: PII detection & anonymization for text and images – protecting personal data
cards.detail:
Presidio is an open-source framework from Microsoft for detecting, redacting, masking and anonymizing sensitive data (PII) in text, images and structured data. Combines NLP (spaCy, transformers), regex patterns, rule-based logic and checksums to identify credit cards, names, addresses, SSNs, emails, phone numbers and many other PII types. Supports multiple languages and can be extended with custom recognizers. Deployable via Python packages or Docker containers, integrates well with LLM pipelines to sanitize data before sending to models.

Works well with: LangChain · LiteLLM · Guardrails AI · NeMo Guardrails
whenToUse: PII detection and anonymization in LLM pipelines
text de-identification before model training or logging
privacy-aware data preprocessing for RAG systems
custom PII recognizer development with NLP/regex
whenNotToUse: real-time high-throughput stream processing without tuning
non-text PII detection (audio, video) beyond image redaction
when only simple regex-based masking is needed

cards.name: Guardrails AI
cards.desc: I/O validation framework for LLMs – structured output + 100+ validators
cards.detail:
Guardrails AI is a Python framework for building reliable AI applications by running Input/Output Guards that detect, measure and mitigate various risk types. Guardrails Hub provides 100+ ready-made validators including: PII detection, toxic language, competitor mentions, bias, prompt injection and many more. Supports validating structured data from LLM output with automatic reask when output fails to meet standards. Can be deployed as a standalone service via REST API, integrates easily with OpenAI, Anthropic, and any LLM provider.

Works well with: LangChain · Presidio · Promptfoo · LiteLLM
whenToUse: structured output validation and type enforcement from LLMs
composable input/output guards with Hub validators
risk detection and mitigation via validator marketplace
LLM reliability improvement with auto-reask on failure
whenNotToUse: conversational flow control (NeMo Guardrails is more suitable)
LLM vulnerability scanning and red-teaming (use garak)
non-Python tech stacks without REST API bridge
